key_insight: ULTRA unifies multimodal perception and high-level task commands into a single whole-body control policy, enabling humanoids to generate autonomous loco-manipulation behavior directly from sensors and instructions rather than tracking predefined motion references.
problem_solved: Overcomes scarcity/low quality of retargeted motion data, limited scalability of skill repertoires, and dependence on reference tracking by producing perception-driven, task-conditioned whole-body behaviors.
method: Train a unified multimodal control policy that maps vision, proprioception, and high-level task specifications to whole‑body commands.
Use hierarchical or modular representations (skill latents / mixture of behaviors) to scale to large repertoires while preserving stable loco-manipulation.
Prioritize generation from perception and task intent instead of retargeting or following pre-recorded motion references, enabling on-the-fly adaptation.
impact: Makes humanoid robots more autonomous and versatile by reducing reliance on motion capture and reference tracking, and by enabling scalable, perception-driven whole-body manipulation for real-world tasks.
visual_elements: System diagram: multimodal inputs (camera, language/task spec, proprioception) → unified policy → whole-body control outputs (actuators).
Before vs After bar/graphic: traditional reference-tracking pipeline vs ULTRA (data efficiency, scalability, autonomy).
Sequence montage: robot performing a range of loco-manipulation tasks generated from perception and high-level commands.
Skill-latent map or modular block diagram showing how many behaviors are covered and how they are composed.
paper_title: ULTRA: Unified Multimodal Control for Autonomous Humanoid Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation
paper_authors: Xialin He, Sirui Xu, Xinyao Li, Runpei Dong, Liuyu Bian
